column1: # Declares which host surfaces this domain OWNS and which it only READS, so
# "cross-domain awareness" is a checked claim instead of prose. `# own` prefixes
# are the surfaces this domain owns outright; every census row outside them must
# be covered by a row below, which names the lane that owns it and the citation
# Columns (row lines): path <TAB> owner <TAB> status <TAB> claim <TAB> basis <TAB> token <TAB> note
#   path   a surface root ($HOME/... or absolute); the longest matching prefix covers a census row
#   owner  a lane id declared by an `# owner` directive. On an `unresolved` row
#          it names the lane that owes the ruling (the arbiter), not a found
#          owner — a single-owner reading of that group is a misreading.
#   claim  presence-only  => every covered census row must carry mode `-`
#          declared       => every covered census row must carry an exact mode
#   basis  a citation that must resolve and whose cited line(s) must match `token`:
#   token  ERE that AT LEAST ONE line of the cited range must match (a `:N-M`
#          citation is satisfied by any matching line in the range; a citation
#          with no `:N` is checked against the whole file). Stated because
#          'every cited line' would be a stricter rule than the one implemented
#          (round-16 planner). ERE the cited line(s) must match, so a basis cannot decay into a
#          pointer at unrelated text (the corpus/README.md:76 class). A token is
#          a floor, not a relevance proof: a line that mentions the surface
#          without asserting a claim still passes (bound 6).
#   note   free text; no secret value, no vault ref path, no account identifier
#   # own <prefix>          this domain owns the prefix (and everything under it)
#   # owner | # status | # claim | # no-enumerate <value>  the closed vocabularies
# `# no-enumerate <dir>` records a directory deliberately NOT scanned: it must be
# a census row or an ancestor of one, and must not be a `# scan` directory.
# Count the directives with `grep -cE '^# own[[:space:]]+.HOME/'` — the prose
# lines in this header also begin with `# own` / `# owner`, so a naive
# `grep -c '^# own'` overcounts (9 rather than 5; ledger row R16-04 pins it).
# Verify: corpus/scope-gate.sh   Re-partition after inspection: an `# own` or
# `# owner` edit is a scope decision, so there is deliberately no `--pin`.
# Rows: 4 groups covering the 8 census rows outside the 5 owned prefixes.
